fix: At each batch boundary (and chain re-entry), when origin/main contains ship-verified commits newer than the running binary's build SHA: rebuild, run the reset-sha integrity flow with an auditable 'boundary-refresh' authorization class (NOT silent), and re-exec the loop. Refuse mid-batch (lanes in flight). Wiring proof: a fixture batch whose main advances mid-batch must relaunch on the new binary at the boundary with the repin ledgered.
notes: Three of this week's halts were binary-lag shaped. The refresh is deterministic operator toil — exactly what Rule 5 says belongs in code.
summary: Overnight 2026-08-05 measured cost: the sentinel tail-anchor fix landed at cycle-1301 (64f8620e) but cycles 1302-1309 kept running the OLD first-match parser — 3 wasted cycles on the audit-warn lane (1298/1308/1309, all parser-distortion casualties) plus the cycle-1309 identical-fingerprint batch HALT, on a defect that was already fixed in the repo. Same shape as the escalation/salvage mechanisms sitting inert for a full day. Every refresh today was manual operator work (rebuild + reset-sha -operator + relaunch).
title: Binary lag: the loop executes a frozen binary while its own fixes land on main — auto rebuild+repin+re-exec at batch boundaries when origin has advanced
